info.title: Yogabase Yogabase Application API
info.description: Target-local Yogabase application-plane API. This contract excludes Yogabase management, delivery, provisioning, CRDs, raw SQL, provider coordinates, and GameSessions. The client-facing Data API, withdrawn on 2026-09-08, was restored by the owner decision of 2026-09-17 in a new shape: /v1/data/{table}/select|insert|upsert|update|delete, served only where the bootstrap document's requested-only data-rest row says so, running under row-level security as the signed-in user. The 2026-09-08 /v1/data/{resource}/* shape with typed value objects does not return.

x-yogabase-data-api.identity: Every request runs in one transaction that switches to the NOLOGIN role yogabase_authenticated (never BYPASSRLS) and sets app.project_id and app.subject_id transaction-locally; policies read current_setting('app.subject_id', true). A table is reachable only when the developer granted it to yogabase_authenticated and it has row-level security enabled; Yogabase's own tables are never reachable.
x-yogabase-data-api.values: Request values are plain JSON. Each travels as an untyped parameter the database parses with the target column's own input function: numbers and strings as written, booleans as true/false, objects and arrays as JSON text for json/jsonb columns, and arrays as array literals for array columns. Rows come back as the database renders them with to_json, timestamps in UTC.

x-yogabase-storage.refusals: Every refusal from /v1/storage/objects/{key} is application/problem+json with a stable code and a fixed detail sentence naming the cause; the detail never quotes the key, the object, or provider output. The caller, key and namespace checks run before the object is looked up, so those refusals are identical whether or not the object exists; only object_not_found (404) and object_conflict (409) depend on it, and their status already says so. A request the gateway cannot authenticate at all is answered 401 before any storage check runs.

gatewayHost.description: The exact TLS gateway origin returned by the client bootstrap document.

presence.description: Available only where the bootstrap document's realtime-presence row, requested through X-Yogabase-Accept-Capabilities, says so. TrackPresence(topic) makes the caller's subject present on the topic and also subscribes the connection to it; UntrackPresence(topic) withdraws presence and leaves the subscription; GetPresence(topic) returns {topic, members:[{subject, connections}], truncated}. The presence client method carries {topic, subject, kind}. Events are delivered at least once across replicas; the snapshot is authoritative.

x-yogabase-inline-payload.payload: A request's payload may be at most maximumPayloadBytes before base64 encoding, sent inline as inlinePayloadBase64 or as the object an objectReference names; the object is held to the same limit, so a payload larger than that is accepted on neither.
x-yogabase-inline-payload.requestBody: The whole request body may be at most maximumRequestBodyBytes. That is the largest compact JSON document the request can be with its payload at the limit, taking each character of a string as the longest escape a JSON writer may use (six bytes), because a payload's bytes decide what its base64 weighs once written: System.Text.Json's default encoder writes a base64 plus sign that way, a random payload gains about 8%, and a payload of nothing but plus signs weighs six times its text. A request at the payload limit is therefore accepted however its bytes encode and whichever JSON writer wrote it.

refusal.description: A payload over the limit, or a body over the largest the route takes, is refused with a problem that names the limits. The status is the same whichever of the two the gateway finds first.

get.description: Resolves secret-free configuration. A publishable key identifies configuration and never authenticates a request. The capabilities array always carries the four core rows; a requested-only row is added only for a client that names it in X-Yogabase-Accept-Capabilities.

post.description: Verifies a local project password and establishes the protected interactive session used by the authorization and MFA endpoints.
Consumes the exact user id and one-time token delivered in the authentication-email action.
Always returns the same accepted response so account existence and throttling are not disclosed.
Consumes the exact user id and one-time token delivered in the authentication-email action.
Returns an authenticator enrollment key only to the protected interactive project session.

200.description: A replacement set of single-use recovery codes.

post.description: Completes a configured external identity flow. The callback never auto-links by email and returns unavailable when no installation verifier exists.

Reads rows of one exposed table under row-level security as the signed-in user. An absent or ["*"] column list means every column the caller may read. One more row than the limit is fetched to set hasMore.
Inserts one to 500 rows. The column list is the union of the rows' keys; a row that leaves a column out takes its default. A policy's WITH CHECK refusal is 403 data_row_not_permitted.
Inserts rows; a conflict on onConflict (the columns of a primary key or unique index) updates every other supplied column, or does nothing with ignoreDuplicates.
Updates the rows the filters and the caller's policies select. At least one filter is required.
Deletes the rows the filters and the caller's policies select. At least one filter is required.

200.description: Object bytes. No digest response header exists in v1, so download integrity verification is not claimed.

post.description: Synchronously invokes one project-scoped Actor Lambda instance. The canonical local subject is carried to customer code; application authorization remains part of the admitted Function contract.
Starts or idempotently replays one exact immutable Workflow definition.
Idempotently cancels and compensates a non-terminal Workflow owned by the same canonical local subject. Arbitrary signals are not part of v1.

Allocates one Ready instance of a hosted service to the signed-in player and returns the address to connect to. The Control Plane decides which instance; the gateway relays. A project with no Ready instance carrying an observed address is refused with server_none_available rather than given an address nothing answers on.

get.description: Every instance of the caller's environment as a bare array, ordered by server id. An instance whose address no member has observed is listed with an empty networkPorts rather than omitted or given a composed host.

200.description: The instances this caller may see.

get.description: One instance of the caller's environment. A server id from another project is answered exactly as one that does not exist.

post.description: Releases the allocation this caller holds on one instance, returning it to the pool. It is never a deletion: retirement is decided by the environment's own capacity policy, and an instance allocated to a different caller is refused with server_stop_not_available.

AcceptCapabilities.name: X-Yogabase-Accept-Capabilities
AcceptCapabilities.description: Comma-separated requested-only capability ids this client can read, today realtime-presence and data-rest. Each id the gateway knows adds its row after the four core rows, available or not; core and unknown ids are ignored, and a value longer than 512 characters is ignored as a whole. A client sends an id only once its own validation accepts that row. A gateway that predates a row ignores the header, which a client reads as that capability being unavailable.

Table.name: table
Table.description: A table in the project's public schema, exactly as the database names it. A name that is not exposed to the caller, and a name that does not exist, are the same 403 data_table_not_exposed.

ServerId.name: serverId
ServerId.description: Opaque game-server instance identifier, as returned by start or list.

ObjectKey.name: key
ObjectKey.description: Project-local logical key. The live route is a catch-all path tail; SDKs must validate the key and percent-encode each segment separately while preserving literal slash separators.

ClientConfigurationNotFound.description: The same response is used for disabled, malformed, and unknown keys.

DataResult.description: The rows (each as the database rendered it) and how many rows the statement touched.

GameServer.description: One game-server instance and the addresses a client may connect to.

InvocationResult.description: Typed invocation outcome. Expected domain failures retain this shape on non-2xx statuses.

WorkflowStartResult.description: The deterministic durable Workflow instance identity.

Unauthorized.description: A valid canonical project bearer subject is required.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request payload is over the inline limit, or the request body is over the largest the route takes. The problem's code is payload_too_large, and it names both limits in bytes: limitBytes for the payload and maxBodyBytes for the whole body.

RateLimited.description: The fixed-window request limit was exceeded.

service.description: Canonical hosted-service id to allocate an instance of.

customData.description: Bounded string map recorded on the allocation and carried to the instance. At most 4096 bytes as canonical JSON. It reaches customer code, so it must never carry a credential or another player's identity.

internalPort.description: Port the workload listens on inside its Pod.

externalPort.description: Port to connect to on host.

host.description: Node address the member observed. Never composed by the Control Plane.

state.description: Lifecycle state, verbatim. Read it as text: a state Yogabase adds later must stay readable rather than fail a client.

networkPorts.description: Empty when no member has observed an address for this instance; a client must not connect to such an instance.

realtimeEndpoint.description: Exact HTTPS origin of the separately deployed SignalR realtime gateway.

oidcRedirectUris.description: Exact OAuth redirect allowlist. Entries are public HTTPS URLs, loopback HTTP URLs, or lowercase reverse-domain private-use native schemes such as com.example.app:/oauth/callback. Userinfo, query strings, and fragments are forbidden.

capabilities.description: The four core rows (auth, storage, functions-rest, realtime-subscribe) in that order, then one row for each requested-only id the client named in X-Yogabase-Accept-Capabilities, in x-yogabase-requested-only order. A client that names nothing receives exactly the four core rows.

id.description: realtime-presence appears only when requested; it is available exactly when realtime-subscribe is and the runtime's realtime projection enables presence. data-rest appears only when requested; it is available exactly when the runtime enables the Data API, which requires auth.

DataColumnList.description: Column names, or ["*"] for every column the caller may read.

value.description: Absent for isNull and notNull; an array of 1-100 non-null values for in; a string pattern for like and ilike; otherwise one non-null JSON value.

DataRow.description: Column name to plain JSON value.

hasMore.description: For a select, true when another page exists past this one.

deadline.description: Must be within 30 seconds of admission.
